HTTP snapshot resolver with peer state, deadlines, sockets, and poll-based refresh logic.

# Purpose
This file implements an HTTP snapshot resolver for a set of peers. It manages peer records in a pool, tracks peer state with deadline lists, and uses non-blocking TCP sockets with `poll()` to fetch snapshot data from each peer. The resolver supports two fetch paths per peer: a full snapshot and an incremental snapshot. It stores the result in `fd_ssresolve_peer_t` and calls the `on_resolve_cb` callback when a peer has finished resolving.

The main public interface is [`fd_http_resolver_new`](<#fd_http_resolver_new>), [`fd_http_resolver_join`](<#fd_http_resolver_join>), [`fd_http_resolver_add`](<#fd_http_resolver_add>), and [`fd_http_resolver_advance`](<#fd_http_resolver_advance>). [`fd_http_resolver_new`](<#fd_http_resolver_new>) allocates and initializes all internal storage, including peer pools, deadline lists, poll arrays, and one `fd_ssresolve` object for each fetch type per peer. [`fd_http_resolver_advance`](<#fd_http_resolver_advance>) drives the state machine: it starts new connections, handles timeouts, processes socket events, moves peers between `unresolved`, `resolving`, `valid`, and `invalid` lists, and removes peers from the selector when they fail.
